verdicts.text: Pulumi provides a `pulumi.StackReference` construct with a `getOutput` method for referencing outputs from another Pulumi stack.
verdicts.evidence: The Node.js SDK defines `export class StackReference extends CustomResource`, described as "Manages a reference to a Pulumi stack". It includes `public getOutput(name: Input<string>): Output<any>`, which "Fetches the value of the named stack output".

verdicts.text: There exists a `terraform.state.S3Reference` construct (in a `@pulumi/terraform`-like package) that can reference Terraform state stored in an S3 bucket by bucket and key, and expose a `getOutput` method to retrieve individual state outputs.
verdicts.evidence: The generated `@pulumi/terraform` Node.js SDK (sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts) exports only invoke functions: `getS3Reference`/`getS3ReferenceOutput`, `getLocalReference`, `getRemoteReference` and `getAzureRMReference` (e.g. "export const getS3Reference: typeof import(\"./getS3Reference\").getS3Reference"). It has no `S3Reference` class that you construct with `new` and that has a `getOutput` method. The docs also use `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` (L203), which doesn't exist either.
verdicts.intuition_flag: This looks like a made-up API. The real way to read S3 state is terraform.state.getS3ReferenceOutput({bucket, key, ...}), which returns outputs, not a `new S3Reference(...)` with `.getOutput()`.

verdicts.text: The `pulumi import` CLI command accepts a syntax of the form `pulumi import <type>:<module>/<resource>:<Resource> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says: "If using the command line args directly, the type token, name, id and optional flags must be provided. For example: pulumi import 'aws:iam/user:User' name id". The example `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345` fits this form.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Small wording issue: the first segment of the placeholder should be <package>, not <type>. The whole string `<package>:<module>/<resource>:<Resource>` is the type token.

verdicts.text: Pulumi Policy as Code (via `@pulumi/policy`'s `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`) can implement infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: The Pulumi Policies overview says: "You define guardrails in code and apply them consistently across resources managed by Pulumi IaC, provisioned with Terraform or CloudFormation, or created manually." Coverage of Terraform resources depends on Audit mode, which "Continuously scans resources discovered through Insights Discovery... including resources created with Terraform." Preventative mode only checks Pulumi stacks during preview/up.
verdicts.framing_note: This is supporting evidence from another Pulumi page, not product source. The claim is true in general, but the example snippet (a mandatory validateResource policy) only blocks Pulumi deployments. It applies to Terraform-created resources only through Insights Discovery in audit mode, which requires Pulumi Cloud, and the page doesn't mention that.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Readers may think the snippet enforces policies during terraform plan/apply. It doesn't: Terraform resources are covered only by audit scans in Pulumi Cloud.

verdicts.text: A Pulumi `PolicyPack` can define a `require-tags` policy with `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` that validates `aws.ec2.Instance` resources for required tags.
verdicts.evidence: The @pulumi/policy source has `export type EnforcementLevel = "advisory" | "mandatory" | "remediate" | "disabled";`. The `Policy` interface includes `name`, `description` and `enforcementLevel?`, and its own docstring example uses `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` with `validateResource: validateResourceOfType(aws.s3.Bucket, ...)`. So the doc's `require-tags` policy, which uses `validateResourceOfType(aws.ec2.Instance, ...)` to check tags, is valid API usage.
verdicts.framing_note: The SDK defines `policies`, `name`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and `validateResourceOfType` for any resource class. The claim is one specific use of that API: a tag-checking policy on `aws.ec2.Instance`.

verdicts.text: `aws.ec2.Instance` resources expose a `tags` property that can be inspected via `validateResourceOfType`.
verdicts.evidence: The generated pulumi-aws Node SDK (sdk/nodejs/ec2/instance.ts) shows `tags` as an Instance argument, e.g. `new aws.ec2.Instance("example", { ... tags: { Name: "HelloWorld" } })`, and the docs note "instance tags — applied to instances". `validateResourceOfType(aws.ec2.Instance, (instance, ...) => ...)` hands the callback the resource's input properties, so `instance.tags` can be read there.
verdicts.framing_note: The fetched output was cut off before the `tags` property declaration. `tags` shows up in the SDK's generated usage examples, and I couldn't reach pulumi-policy source because of a rate limit.

verdicts.text: `aws.s3.Bucket` resources expose an `acl` property that can take values such as `"public-read"` or `"public-read-write"`.
verdicts.evidence: pulumi-aws sdk/nodejs/s3/bucket.ts declares `acl: pulumi.Output<string>`, and its doc comment says "Valid values are `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `aws-exec-read`, `authenticated-read`, and `log-delivery-write`." The property is marked "@deprecated acl is deprecated. Use the aws.s3.BucketAcl resource instead." A policy that only checks `bucket.acl` would miss buckets made public through a separate BucketAcl resource.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The `acl` property is deprecated in favor of aws.s3.BucketAcl, so the example policy may not catch every public bucket.
